headline: Brazil Freezes Discord Live Tools
deck: Brazil’s data authority ordered Discord to switch off Go Live and equivalent live-video features inside the country. The rest of the platform stays online; the tools return only after safeguards and prior clearance.
body: Brazil’s National Data Protection Authority ordered Discord to suspend the Go Live feature and functionally equivalent live-video tools for users in Brazilian territory inside the closed-server environment [E1]. The determination leaves every other part of the service intact. Discord must demonstrate that the suspension is fully in place within three business days of notification [E1]. The measure targets the specific affordance that the authority found carrying robust evidence of severe risk to users under eighteen [E1].

Reactivation of the live tools, total or partial, requires Discord to prove the adoption and effectiveness of adequate technical, security and governance measures [E1]. Only after that demonstration may the company seek express prior authorization from the authority. Until those conditions are satisfied the suspension remains in force [E1]. The order sits inside a fiscalization process opened under the Digital Statute of the Child and Adolescent [E1].

National law attaches to a feature that is distributed through global accounts, servers, viewers and technical routes. Compliance therefore includes the construction of technically effective anti-evasion mechanisms that keep the suspended tools offline for Brazilian users no matter how the signal is routed [E1]. The authority made that anti-circumvention duty part of the preventive measure itself. The obligation travels with the feature rather than with any single server location [E1].

SaferNet Brasil processed 406 reports involving Discord in the first seven months of 2026 [E2]. Those filings supply the risk context that framed the authority’s decision. The number records reports, not adjudicated incidents, and offers no denominator for Discord’s full Brazilian user base. The same organization has documented a multi-year rise in Discord-related complaints [E2].

Protection of minors accounts for approximately 41 percent of the moderation decisions Discord itself reported to the European Digital Services Act transparency database [E3]. That share, drawn from more than twenty-five million unique statements of reasons, underscores the volume of child-safety traffic the platform already flags [E3]. The technical note that produced the figure covers the period through early August 2026 [E3].

Disabling one live-video affordance can displace abuse into other channels that remain open on the same closed servers. The preventive measure has not yet generated outcome data showing whether the targeted harm actually declines. Discord retains the right to file an administrative appeal within ten business days and thereafter to seek review by the directing council [E1]. The counter-case therefore remains live on both practical and procedural grounds.

The order establishes a feature-level precedent: a national regulator can attach binding obligations to one live-video tool distributed through a global service without taking the entire platform offline [E1]. That distinction keeps the intervention narrow and leaves the broader service available. Whether the approach ultimately reduces risk or merely relocates it is an empirical question the coming months will test.
